input.quote: provided that (a) M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement pursuant to a merger in which Customer is a party and as a result of which the surviving corporation becomes an Affiliate of another bank holding company, bank, savings and loan association or other financial institution having a capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000 so long as the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with and (b) M&I may freely assign this Agreement
input.rationale: Section 22.4 fails the fallback on three material terms. (1) M&I may "freely assign" in any merger, reorganization or sale of assets, stock or securities, while Customer's consent-free carve-out reaches only a merger in which the survivor becomes an Affiliate of a financial institution with capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000, so an acquisition or sale of substantially all of Customer's assets to any other successor needs consent. (2) Neither party's successor assignment carries a written-notice mechanic. (3) Clause (b)(ii) let M&I assign without our consent "to any entity which is a successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division of M&I" — a partial/divisional transfer rather than succession to M&I itself, so the general consent sentence did not in fact reach every non-successor assignment. Our single edit broadens Customer's carve-out (mirroring M&I's "assets, stock or securities" framing, consistent with the fallback's mutual-successor position), adds the mutual written-notice condition, removes "freely" so M&I's carve-out is consistent with that condition, and deletes (b)(ii); the "not be unreasonably withheld" standard and the Section 21.11 cross-reference are retained untouched. We did not pursue preferred (Customer affiliate carve-out, no consent-free Vendor assignment, competitor bar), which would require deleting M&I's assignment rights and collateral rewrites; the preferred change-of-control element is already satisfied by Section 21.11.B ("M&I agrees to continue to provide Services under this Agreement"), which caps M&I's obligation at pre-change volumes plus 25% but gives it no termination right, and Section 11.3 is redacted but appears from the Section 11.1 fee carve-out to be a Customer right.

mappings.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
A successor assignment requires written notice.
Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
mappings.quote: which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld

proposal.summary: Mutual successor assignment on written notice; delete M&I's consent-free divisional-transfer exception
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our fallback position is a mutual right to assign to a successor on written notice, with consent (not unreasonably withheld) for all other assignments. We broadened Customer's carve-out from mergers with $100,000,000 financial institutions to any successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, made both parties' successor assignments subject to written notice, and deleted M&I's consent-free right to transfer the Agreement to a purchaser of its Data Services division, which is a partial-business transfer rather than a successor to M&I.

ops.oldText: provided that (a) M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement pursuant to a merger in which Customer is a party and as a result of which the surviving corporation becomes an Affiliate of another bank holding company, bank, savings and loan association or other financial institution having a capital and surplus of at least $100,000,000 so long as the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with and (b) M&I may freely assign this Agreement (i) in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities, or (ii) to any entity which is a successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division of M&I.
ops.newText: provided that, in each case upon written notice to the other party, (a) M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets, stock or securities, so long as the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with, and (b) M&I may assign this Agreement in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities.
